copy.intro: A curated inventory of the source datasets and pipeline products behind single-structure and WUI fire-risk work, with provider, purpose, coverage, vintage, limitations and documentation.
aboutParagraphs: Each card is a dataset: a source product or a family of related products used or considered in the fire-risk workflows. One card can span several vintages, geographies or related products.

“Used for” shows which model variable a dataset feeds. A dashed “supporting” label marks context data that is not confirmed as an input to a variable. Check each record’s scope and data notes before using it.

Source links point to the provider’s own documentation, not necessarily the exact release, licence or processing used in the pipeline. Confirm version, geography, method and permitted use before interpretation or redistribution.

Pipeline products are outputs generated by the fire-risk pipeline (for example fire frequency, damage predictions, imputed values and the WUI exposure index). They are stored in the project S3 bucket, are not public and have no source links.
Data formats in this inventory: CSV, Excel workbooks, File Geodatabase, GeoJSON, GeoPackage, GeoTIFF and other rasters, NetCDF, Parquet, and Shapefile. Some sources are distributed as ZIP archives.
copy.footer: Single-Structure & WUI Fire Risk Data Inventory
copy.scopeSummary: Fire history, buildings and property, people and resilience, weather, fuels and wildfire hazard, plus the pipeline products built from them. Each dataset shows which model variable it feeds.
copy.noDictionaryMatch: No direct match in the MAIN DICTIONARY; this source is listed for reference and is not confirmed as an index input.
copy.noSourceLinks: No documentation links are listed for this source.

dictionaryRecords.name: NFIRS Fire Incidents
dictionaryRecords.description: Structure-fire incident records used for historical fire frequency and property-loss calculations.
dictionaryRecords.pipeline: The dictionary lists NFIRS as the source for annualized fire frequency and identifies NFIRS incident-level fire records as a pipeline input.
dictionaryRecords.scope: U.S. fire-department reports; voluntary participation and reporting vary by year and jurisdiction.
dictionaryRecords.qualification: NFIRS is not a census of all U.S. fire incidents. USFA warns that raw records should not be used as simple counts of fires, deaths, injuries or dollar loss. The workbook period ends in 2025; confirm the selected tables, reporting years and filters.
dictionaryRecords.sourceNote: The workbook points to annual NFIRS public data. It does not specify the exact release files or extracted incident fields.

dictionaryRecords.name: NFIRS Casualties
dictionaryRecords.description: Civilian and firefighter casualty records used to estimate injury and loss-of-life values.
dictionaryRecords.pipeline: Used with NFIRS incident data to value fatalities and injuries; the workbook describes severity-specific injury valuation.
dictionaryRecords.scope: U.S. voluntary incident-reporting system; casualty data completeness varies.
dictionaryRecords.qualification: Casualty tables are related records in a multi-table reporting system. Linkage keys, missing casualty reporting, year coverage and severity field mappings should be checked in the actual extract.
dictionaryRecords.sourceNote: The dictionary identifies NFIRS casualty records but does not list the extracted fields or specific release files.

dictionaryRecords.name: American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates
dictionaryRecords.description: Socioeconomic and population estimates used in population exposure and the Area Deprivation Index (ADI) workflow.
dictionaryRecords.pipeline: The dictionary cites ACS for Census population and ADI inputs. ACS 5-year profiles provide demographic, social, economic and housing measures across small-area geographies.
dictionaryRecords.scope: U.S. geographies down to census tracts; table and geography availability depend on the ACS product.
dictionaryRecords.qualification: Confirm the ACS release, table IDs, estimates, margins of error, geography and population universe used by the pipeline. The workbook references ACS 2022 but does not list table or field IDs.
dictionaryRecords.sourceNote: The exact 5-year ACS product (detailed tables, profiles, or other) and variables have not been identified in the dictionary.
dictionaryRecords.keywords: American Community Survey census population demographics ADI

dictionaryRecords.name: Census TIGER/Line geography
dictionaryRecords.description: Census geographic boundary files cited for population inputs and spatial assignment.
dictionaryRecords.pipeline: The workbook links Census TIGER/Line files as an original source for Census population inputs. Boundary vintages are needed to join population and block-group-level risk outputs.
dictionaryRecords.scope: U.S. statistical and legal boundaries; TIGER/Line products are released by year and geography.
dictionaryRecords.qualification: No vintage, geometry level, relationship file or specific TIGER/Line product is identified. Match boundary vintage and geographic identifiers to the ACS estimates before spatial joins.
dictionaryRecords.sourceNote: The workbook gives the Census TIGER download portal, but not a specific year or boundary file.
dictionaryRecords.keywords: TIGER shapefile boundaries block group geography

dictionaryRecords.name: Parcel assessment & building value data
dictionaryRecords.description: Assessed improvement values associated with parcels, adjusted to fire-year dollars using the FHFA House Price Index (HPI).
dictionaryRecords.pipeline: The dictionary describes LightBox assessed improvement values and FHFA-adjusted values for building replacement-cost and exposure calculations.
dictionaryRecords.scope: Parcel and property attributes; LightBox product coverage and update schedules vary by product and release.
dictionaryRecords.qualification: The source record does not identify a LightBox product edition, geography, data currency date, extracted columns or license. LightBox data is commercial; verify internal entitlement and redistribution restrictions. FHFA HPI tracks home-price changes and should not be assumed to reproduce local assessed-value changes without checking the pipeline method.
dictionaryRecords.sourceNote: Workbook wording: LightBox assessed improvement values adjusted to fire-year dollars using FHFA HPI. It also references GlobalBuildingAtlas for building data.
dictionaryRecords.keywords: property parcel assessment improvements values exposure FHFA HPI

dictionaryRecords.name: GlobalBuildingAtlas (GBA)
dictionaryRecords.description: Global building footprints, building heights and Level of Detail 1 building models cited by the dictionary.
dictionaryRecords.pipeline: The workbook references GlobalBuildingAtlas alongside parcel data and building value calculations. The precise GBA component used by the pipeline is not specified.
dictionaryRecords.scope: Global building-level geographic coverage; available layers and attributes vary by component.
dictionaryRecords.qualification: The project describes multiple components with distinct licensing: ODbL polygons, and CC BY-NC 4.0 polygons, LoD1 models and height maps. Identify the exact component before use or redistribution; do not infer that all components have the same license.
dictionaryRecords.sourceNote: Included because the workbook links to GBA; the exact layer or file used by the pipeline is not identified.

dictionaryRecords.name: Value of Statistical Life (VSL) series
dictionaryRecords.provider: Internal series; upstream source not identified
dictionaryRecords.description: Annual VSL values used to monetize fatalities and injury severity, and population exposure.
dictionaryRecords.pipeline: The workbook names vsl_smoothed.csv and describes annual VSL estimates for fatality, injury and population-exposure calculations.
dictionaryRecords.scope: Annual values; currency year, geography and assumptions are not specified in the workbook.
dictionaryRecords.qualification: The external source, value series, smoothing method, base year, inflation adjustment and adult/child assumptions are not documented. The EPA reference below is general mortality-risk valuation guidance, not confirmation of the pipeline's VSL series or method.
dictionaryRecords.sourceNote: The only named source is the internal filename vsl_smoothed.csv. Confirm its origin, version and calculation notes with the pipeline owner.
dictionaryRecords.keywords: VSL statistical life fatality injury annual monetization

dictionaryRecords.name: Baseline Resilience Indicators for Communities (BRIC)
dictionaryRecords.provider: University of South Carolina, Hazards & Vulnerability Research Institute
dictionaryRecords.description: County-level community resilience index used as an indicator in the Community Risk Factor (CRF).
dictionaryRecords.pipeline: The dictionary describes BRIC as a resilience indicator assigned to block groups by county and references BRIC in CRF calculation.
dictionaryRecords.scope: County-level index for U.S. communities; project reports 2010, 2015 and 2020 vintages, with geographic coverage varying by vintage.
dictionaryRecords.qualification: BRIC is a county composite, not a block-group measurement. The workbook notes CRF as ADI ÷ BRIC and mentions BRIC/CRCI; verify the exact BRIC release, field, scaling and formula before interpreting the resulting CRF.
dictionaryRecords.sourceNote: The workbook links the BRIC project page but does not specify the score field or product vintage.

dictionaryRecords.name: Area Deprivation Index (ADI)
dictionaryRecords.description: Block-group deprivation indicator calculated from ACS 5-year socioeconomic measures using the pysociome ADI methodology.
dictionaryRecords.pipeline: The dictionary lists ADI as an intermediate measure and describes it as one component of the Community Risk Factor.
dictionaryRecords.scope: Census block-group level as described by the workbook; source vintage and version are unspecified.
dictionaryRecords.qualification: This is a derived index, not a raw input dataset. The workbook does not identify the exact ACS fields, code/version, scale, normalization or output vintage. The Neighborhood Atlas is the ADI reference; confirm whether the pipeline's custom pysociome calculation matches the published ADI methodology.
dictionaryRecords.sourceNote: The workbook says ADI is calculated from ACS using pysociome methodology and marks it as not included in the final output.
dictionaryRecords.keywords: area deprivation index ADI ACS socioeconomic block group

records.name: Baseline Resilience Indicators for Communities (BRIC)
records.description: County-level resilience score workbooks referenced by the dictionary for the Community Risk Factor.
records.pipeline: Community resilience scores that are an input to the community risk factor (CRF).
records.scope: County scores; the workbook describes county-level BRIC values assigned to block groups.
records.qualification: Confirm the workbook vintage, score field and geographic join used. BRIC measures county resilience; it is not itself a block-group measure.

records.name: Census ACS and TIGER/Line
records.description: ACS 5-year estimates and Census geographic files, including population, ADI/BRIC-related tables and boundary data.
records.pipeline: ACS 5-year adult and child population per block group drives population exposure (Ep); the area deprivation index is an input to the community risk factor (CRF); TIGER/Line block groups (2024) are the geography of all results.
records.scope: ACS 5-year estimates span 2013–2024; TIGER/Line geography spans 2019, 2020, 2024 and 2025. Product and geographic level vary.
records.qualification: Dataset labels do not establish which table, field or ACS vintage is consumed by a given run. Match ACS and TIGER/Line vintages and GEOIDs before joining; inspect the specific data schema.

records.name: CAL FIRE Damage Inspection (DINS)
records.description: California post-fire structure inspection records and a Parquet derivative with structure type.
records.pipeline: Observed building damage classes and assessed values for California WUI fires (2013–2025). These also train the DINS-ML (XGBoost) damage model that predicts damage-class probabilities for buildings outside California, feeding property loss (Lp).
records.scope: CAL FIRE inspections of structures affected by wildland fires within or near State Responsibility Area fire perimeters.
records.qualification: CAL FIRE notes that access and fire damage limit inspections and some affected structures may be missed.

records.name: FHFA House Price Index (HPI)
records.description: FHFA House Price Index tables referenced in the dictionary for adjusting assessed improvements to fire-year dollars.
records.pipeline: House price index used to step 2025 building values back to each fire year, so property loss (Lp) and building exposure (Eb) are in fire-year dollars.
records.scope: County, state and census-tract index files.
records.qualification: The HPI measures changes in single-family home prices; confirm the selected index, geography, period and adjustment formula used in the pipeline.

records.name: Fire Weather Index (FWI) grids
records.description: CONUS daily Fire Weather Index grids derived from ERA5-Land. Includes the FWI System codes and indices (FFMC, DMC, DC, ISI, BUI, FWI) and the noon temperature, relative humidity and wind speed and daily precipitation used as inputs.
records.pipeline: Daily fire weather that is an input to the WUI exposure index (WEI).
records.scope: CONUS, 0.1° grid (about 10 km), daily values for 2010–2025.
records.qualification: Derived product (ERA5-Land inputs, not the raw reanalysis). The FWI processing code and version are not recorded in the source documentation.

records.name: Geographic Area Coordination Center boundaries
records.description: Polygon boundaries for the Geographic Area Coordination Centers (GACCs).
records.pipeline: Reference data on this topic; it is not listed among the inputs to the pipeline variables.
records.scope: United States coordination-area polygons.
records.qualification: Boundaries support administrative/fire-response geography; the source disclaims guarantees of accuracy or completeness.

supportingUse.name: Fire-response geography
supportingUse.definition: Coordination-area boundaries for administrative and fire-response context. Not confirmed as an input to a pipeline variable.

records.name: Interagency Fire Perimeter History (IFPH)
records.vintage: Product documentation through 2019; data label through 2025
records.description: Interagency historical wildland fire perimeters in a single large GeoJSON.
records.pipeline: One of three sources combined into de-duplicated wildfire perimeters (1984–2025). Perimeters identify WUI fires, set WUI fire frequency (X) and pair fires with buildings for property loss (Lp).
records.scope: Interagency historical perimeters; source documentation describes IFPH coverage through the 2019 fire season.
records.qualification: The dataset label extends to 2025, while NIFC documentation describes IFPH coverage through 2019. Verify the actual fire-year range and do not assume complete 2020–2025 coverage; NIFC directs users to WFIGS for later years.

records.name: InFORM Fire Occurrence Data Records
records.description: The Fire Occurrence Data Record (FODR) produced by the Interagency Fire Occurrence Reporting Modules (InFORM) application. It is the authoritative fire occurrence dataset for the five major federal fire management agencies and some state agencies, and also includes records bulk-uploaded by non-InFORM state agencies, giving a comprehensive fire occurrence dataset for the United States.
records.pipeline: Fire occurrence records used to calculate annualized WUI fire frequency (X).
records.scope: CONUS fire occurrence reported by participating agencies.
records.qualification: Incorporation of all available historical data is still in progress, so older years may be incomplete. The NIFC page lists no license; confirm permission and terms before reuse.

sources.label: NIFC: InFORM Fire Occurrence Data Records

records.name: LightBox parcel and building data
records.description: State-partitioned parcel and building polygons, centroids, attributes and imputation inputs.
records.pipeline: Building footprints and tax-assessed improvement values (2025), imputed where missing. Building value drives property loss (Lp) and building exposure (Eb).
records.scope: U.S. parcel and building data; geographic coverage and attributes vary by product and release.
records.qualification: LightBox is a commercial provider. Verify the product edition, geography, data currency date, extracted columns and permitted use against the LightBox agreement. The workbook also references GlobalBuildingAtlas, but does not identify the exact component used.

records.name: Monitoring Trends in Burn Severity (MTBS)
records.description: Burn-severity raster layers and a fire-perimeter dataset for large U.S. fires.
records.pipeline: Fire perimeters (1984–2025) used to find WUI fires and set frequency (X), plus burn severity mosaics (2013–2025) that are inputs to the damage model for property loss (Lp).
records.scope: United States; MTBS maps location, extent and severity for large fires.
records.qualification: Assessment timing and methods vary by landscape and product. The 2026 MTBS portal describes both initial and extended assessments; check per-year product status and distinguish MTBS from provisional products.

records.name: Montana Cadastral
records.provider: Montana State Library / Montana Department of Revenue
records.formats: File geodatabase (distributed as a ZIP archive)
records.description: A dated Montana cadastral parcel archive, delivered as a zipped file geodatabase.
records.pipeline: Montana state assessor values that replace LightBox improvement values in Montana, feeding property loss (Lp) and building exposure (Eb).
records.scope: Montana parcel and land-record geography.
records.qualification: The archive's exact included layers, schema, tax year and use terms should be confirmed from its metadata.

records.name: National Fire Incident Reporting System (NFIRS)
records.description: Geocoded annual NFIRS public data releases, one GeoPackage for each year from 2014 through 2025.
records.pipeline: Wildland incident records (2014–2025) with civilian and firefighter injuries and deaths of WUI fires, valued for casualty loss (Lc).
records.scope: U.S. fire-department reports in the voluntary NFIRS reporting system.
records.qualification: NFIRS is not a census of all incidents; reporting participation, casualty records and losses vary. USFA warns against treating raw NFIRS as simple counts of fires, deaths, injuries or dollar loss. NFIRS was decommissioned in January 2026; 2025 was its final PDR year.

records.name: National Structure Inventory (NSI) 2022
records.description: A 2022 point-based structure inventory with a state-level missingness summary.
records.pipeline: Reference data on this topic; it is not listed among the inputs to the pipeline variables.
records.scope: U.S. structure inventory; geographic coverage in this extract is not fully documented.
records.qualification: The NSI is a modeled/compiled inventory whose inputs and quality vary. Confirm which state files and attributes are used; the workbook does not name NSI.

supportingUse.name: Structure inventory
supportingUse.definition: Point-based structure inventory used as a supporting reference for building attributes. Not confirmed as an input to a pipeline variable.

records.name: US State Boundaries
records.description: Cartographic boundary files are simplified representations of selected geographic areas from the Census Bureau's MAF/TIGER geographic database, designed for small-scale thematic mapping.
records.pipeline: State outlines used as base geography for data visualization and maps.
records.scope: United States states and equivalents, generalized at 1:5,000,000.
records.qualification: Generalized for small-scale mapping, so boundaries are simplified and not suited to parcel- or structure-level spatial analysis. This is the 2018 vintage; do not assume it matches later TIGER/Line geography.

records.name: USA Structures (structure type)
records.description: State/territory-partitioned USA Structures building footprint and attribution data.
records.pipeline: Structure type attributes used for data imputation where building information is missing.
records.scope: USA Structures coverage is nationwide, including states and territories.
records.qualification: FEMA describes USA Structures as buildings larger than 450 square feet and updates the product annually. Verify the specific release and structure-type field definition.

records.name: USGS wildfire building loss and perimeters
records.description: Wildfire building loss/exposure points, event summary, perimeter data and a data dictionary.
records.pipeline: Wildfire building loss and perimeter data used in damage modeling, which feeds property loss (Lp).
records.scope: CONUS wildfires from 2002–2022; the source release maps major fires meeting its inclusion criteria.
records.qualification: The USGS release describes buildings exposed to or destroyed by selected destructive wildfires, not all U.S. fires or structures. Check the source's event-selection criteria and the data dictionary.

sources.label: USGS data release: wildfire building destruction and exposure

records.name: WFIGS Interagency Fire Perimeters
records.description: Interagency wildland fire perimeters from the WFIGS product.
records.pipeline: One of three sources combined into de-duplicated wildfire perimeters (1984–2025). Perimeters identify WUI fires, set WUI fire frequency (X) and pair fires with buildings for property loss (Lp).
records.scope: United States; WFIGS describes best-available interagency fire perimeter data.
records.qualification: WFIGS distinguishes current, year-to-date and historical products and applies inclusion/fall-off rules. Confirm whether this is a static historical release or a filtered current service.

records.name: Wildfire Hazard Potential (WHP) 2023
records.description: The 2023 Wildfire Hazard Potential geodatabase.
records.pipeline: Landscape wildfire hazard that is an input to the WUI exposure index (WEI).
records.scope: National wildfire hazard potential at 270 m; the product is intended for relative comparisons.
records.qualification: WHP is a modeled index with uncertainty, not a parcel-level prediction or locally calibrated assessment. Read the product metadata and scale limitations before use.

sources.label: Forest Service Research Data Archive: WHP 2023

records.name: USA Wildlands and WUI Vector Tiles V2
records.formats: File Geodatabase (vector tile layer and WUI zone layers)
records.description: A vector tile layer depicting wildland-urban interface, ember zone, and wildland areas, published with WUI zone layers for the vector tile package.
records.pipeline: WUI interface and intermix zones are used in the WUI exposure index (WEI) and to select the NFIRS incidents counted in casualty loss (Lc).
records.scope: United States wildland, wildland-urban interface and ember zone areas.
records.qualification: Verify which feature classes and zone layers are used in the pipeline.

sources.label: FEMA Hub: USA Wildlands and WUI Vector Tiles V2

records.name: LANDFIRE fuels, vegetation and events
records.provider: U.S. Geological Survey / USDA Forest Service
records.description: LANDFIRE fuel-model, vegetation-cover/height and disturbance/event products across multiple vintages.
records.pipeline: Reference data on this topic; it is not listed among the inputs to the pipeline variables.
records.scope: CONUS vegetation/fuels products and event polygons; extent and layer vary by product/version.
records.qualification: LANDFIRE products are versioned and include modeled/derived layers. Select matched vintage, region and layer; Public Events combines event data from multiple contributors and is not a complete record of every disturbance.

supportingUse.name: Fuels and vegetation
supportingUse.definition: Fuel-model, vegetation and disturbance layers used as supporting hazard context. Not confirmed as an input to a pipeline variable.

variables.name: WUI fire frequency
variables.definition: Distinct fire perimeters within 0.5 mile of a block group in 1984–2025, divided by 42 years.

variables.name: Property loss
variables.definition: Building value in the fire year times damage share, summed over buildings reached by a WUI fire.

variables.name: Casualty loss
variables.definition: NFIRS injuries and deaths valued with the value of a statistical life of the incident year.

variables.name: Building exposure
variables.definition: Total improvement value of the block group in the fire year.

variables.name: Population exposure
variables.definition: Adults counted once and children twice at the value of a statistical life.

variables.name: WUI exposure index
variables.definition: Index (0–100) combining wildfire hazard, fire weather and WUI zone exposure.

variables.name: Community risk factor
variables.definition: Factor from the area deprivation index and community resilience, weighted by the loss of each fire year.

variables.name: Result geography
variables.definition: Block-group geography on which all results are reported.

variables.name: Data imputation
variables.definition: Filling in missing building attributes, such as structure type, before values and losses are calculated.

variables.name: Data visualization
variables.definition: Base geography used to display and map results.
